title: Nuclear War in 2026: What's the REAL Risk Right Now? | Mark Rush, After the Flash
summary: A nuclear survival author tells a prepper channel that Iran was weeks from a bomb, the US faces little direct nuclear risk, and the real threat from the 2026 Iran war is a Strait of Hormuz energy shock.

assertions.quote: they are probably close within a month of being able to build a nuclear weapon.

verdicts.note: Before the June 2025 strikes Iran held over 400 kg of 60 percent enriched uranium, 'enough to build several nuclear weapons'; the strikes' damage and the material's fate are unclear, so nearness to a weapon is uncertain.

assertions.quote: they've responded by making it difficult to transit the Strait of Hormuz, which is playing havoc if you've been to the gas station
there is no evidence to show that they have the ability to hit the United States.

verdicts.note: Iran has no intercontinental missile; US intelligence judges it could develop one only years from now.
US intelligence says that before the 2026 war Iran had only space-launch vehicles it could turn into a military ICBM by 2035 if it chose to, so it had no missile able to reach the US.

assertions.quote: right now roughly 20% of all the world's crude oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz.

verdicts.note: The EIA puts about a fifth of world petroleum liquids and a similar share of LNG trade through the strait.

assertions.quote: So, we have a pretty big buffer just because a lot of the production is here

verdicts.note: US production protects supply, but oil is priced globally, so US fuel prices still rise with a Gulf disruption.
Iran's closure of Hormuz raised energy prices in the US in an election year and strained the US economy, a pressure that helped push Trump to a ceasefire.
